The main takeaway from our work is that

there are wild species of Aegilop and Triticum which have much higher iron and zinc in their grains and that these traits can be transferred to bread and durum cultivar using conventional breeding approaches.
the Aegilops accessions and wild wheat species are rich sources of micronutrients and can be utilized to enhance iron and zinc content of wheat grains through breeding.
there is a great potential of enhancing grain iron and zinc in the elite wheat varieties through conventional breeding by using the wild relatives of wheat and Aegilop species.
